c2add1207d1b0046: OSLO, Oct 9 — South African human rights lawyer Navi Pillay, who challenged apartheid before helping establish rape as an act of genocide under international law, has won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.

The Norwegian Nobel Committee announced the award today, recognising the 85-year-old former United Nations human rights chief for her decades of work defending fundamental rights and advancing international justice.
Pillay, whose full name is Navanethem Pillay, was honoured for her contributions to international law, justice and accountability for some of the world’s gravest crimes.
Her career has taken her from defending anti-apartheid activists in South Africa to serving as a judge in international courts dealing with genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity.

Born in 1941 into a family of Indian descent in Durban, South Africa, Pillay grew up under apartheid, the system of institutionalised racial segregation that denied the country’s non-white population basic rights.

In 1967, she became the first woman to establish a law practice in South Africa’s Natal province, defending anti-apartheid activists and challenging discriminatory conditions in the country’s prisons.
She later became South Africa’s first black woman High Court judge, marking another milestone in a legal career that would extend well beyond her home country.
Following the end of apartheid, Pillay served as a judge at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, established to prosecute those responsible for the 1994 genocide.
There, she helped establish landmark legal precedents recognising that rape and sexual violence could constitute genocide under international law.
The precedent marked a significant development in the prosecution of wartime sexual violence, strengthening international legal protections for victims.
Pillay subsequently served as a judge at the International Criminal Court before becoming UN High Commissioner for Human Rights in 2008, a position she held until 2014.
In that role, she spoke out against human rights abuses and pressed governments to uphold their obligations under international law.

More recently, Pillay chaired a UN commission investigating alleged human rights violations in Israel and the occupied Palestinian territories, placing her once again at the centre of international scrutiny over accountability and the protection of civilians.
The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded annually to individuals or organisations recognised for their contributions to peace.
This year’s award carries prize money of 12 million Swedish kronor, an increase of one million kronor from last year.
Pillay succeeds Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, who won the 2025 prize for her efforts to promote democratic rights in Venezuela.
The award will be formally presented in Oslo on December 10, the anniversary of the death of Alfred Nobel, the Swedish inventor and philanthropist who established the prizes.
64e0cee5f8599fd4: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's successful hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia demonstrates how unity and close cooperation among its multiracial population remain key strengths in achieving excellence on the international stage, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the smooth running of the prestigious motorsport event reflected the dedication of thousands of volunteers, civil servants and Formula 1 personnel who worked together to ensure its success.
"I would like to express my deepest appreciation to everyone who played a role in ensuring that the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 in Malaysia ran smoothly and successfully.
"In addition to F1 personnel, the event was made possible by thousands of volunteers and civil servants.

"This shows that when we work together in a spirit of 'segulai sejalai' (unity), Malaysia can achieve success on the international stage," he said before tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
The 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix, held from Oct 2 to 4, marked F1's return to Sepang after a nine-year absence. The last race at the circuit was held in 2017.

Meanwhile, Anwar said the same spirit of unity was evident in Malaysia's performance at the 20th Asian Games, where the national contingent equalled its best-ever gold medal haul, with athletes from various ethnic backgrounds contributing to the achievement.
"The same applies to the 20th Asian Games, where we matched our best-ever achievement.
"The medal winners came from various ethnic backgrounds, showing that we achieve the best when we draw on the strengths of every community," he said.
Malaysia ended its Asian Games campaign with nine gold, seven silver and 16 bronze medals.
The gold medals came from squash, karate, esports, sepak takraw and track cycling. - Bernama
347f8d4a409abdc5: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will continue the My50 travel pass, benefiting 300,000 users of Prasarana's bus and rail services in the Klang Valley, while introducing the MYKOMUTER50 pass for 40,000 KTM Komuter users.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this when tabling the 2027 Budget today.
He said the initiatives were expected to help commuters save up to RM160 a month on average.
Free travel passes would also be provided to 360,000 beneficiaries, including school students, persons with disabilities and children aged below six.
Anwar said the public had recently faced frequent train breakdowns and service disruptions, affecting their journeys to work.
"Therefore, Prasarana and Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd have been tasked with taking immediate measures to ensure smooth train operations," said Anwar, who is also the finance minister.
As a long-term solution, Prasarana is investing more than RM3.4 billion in a comprehensive rehabilitation of its rail services, he said.
He added that the government would also acquire 42 new train sets for the Electric Train Service and KTM Komuter services.
f72ec8f439f79b2b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) should be seen as part of a “Waad Nasional” or national promise and a national responsibility that must receive a national response, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today in his Budget 2027 speech.

Referring to the agreement which was signed between the founding partners of Malaysia, Anwar said that 12 items under MA63 have been finalised so far, and also listed other measures and allocations that the federal government has been channelling to Sabah and Sarawak.
Anwar said the federal government has agreed to increase Public Service Department (JPA) scholarship offers to Sabah and Sarawak’s students.
“This means 4,200 Sabahans and Sarawakians will get the opportunity to further their studies every year,” he said in the Dewan Rakyat.
In his speech, Anwar noted that the federal government’s special grants over the past decades for Sabah and Sarawak had not been in line with their developmental needs.

He said the current federal government has increased these special grants three times, with the latest interim payment being RM1.5 billion, and that there would be continued talks with Sabah and Sarawak to finalise a fair and sustainable annual formula.

Among the 12 items in MA63 which had been finalised under the current government are permanent representatives from Sabah and Sarawak in the Inland Revenue Board and the Bintulu port becoming a Sarawak-owned port.

They also include Sarawak taking over MASWings, which is now known as AirBorneo, while the federal government still provides RM209 million in subsidies to benefit 820,000 passengers in the interiors; and handing over electricity regulatory powers to Sabah while the federal government continues providing RM600 million to ensure continued electricity supply.

Anwar said the proposed federal allocation for Sabah and Sarawak next year remains the highest, with Sabah to receive RM18.7 billion in 2027 (as compared to RM17.6 billion this year) and Sarawak to receive RM16.2 billion (as compared to RM15.1 billion).
Among other things, Anwar said RM3.3 billion has been allocated next year to continue road and highway projects in Sabah and Sarawak.

Noting that the Sarawak state government has expressed intent to develop a special economic zone in Sibu, Anwar said the federal government has started official talks to finalise the framework for incentives, one-stop centre to facilitate investments and strategic infrastructure needs.
07f5c8ef25b01878: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — More than 9,000 contract doctors will be given permanent posting in public healthcare facilities next year, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.

While tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said the government has offered permanent positions for more than 15,000 contract doctors since 2023, including 4,000 doctors this year alone.
“This means that after this, doctors who complete their housemanship will be offered permanent positions as medical officers,” Anwar said.

Under Budget 2027, the government will also increase post-basic incentives from RM100 to RM200 a month for some 47,000 nurses and paramedics and raise the incentive for Air Health Service staff from RM30 to RM100.
28b722bac3ffcf6c: KUALA LUMPUR: Government-linked investment companies (GLICs) will mobilise RM25 billion in domestic investments under the GEAR-uP initiative to strengthen local companies and expand Malaysia's presence in high-value industries.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said approved investments reached RM218.5 billion in the first half of 2026, an increase of 11.7 per cent, putting Malaysia on track to achieve a new record for the third consecutive year.
He said start-ups must have access to funding from the early stages through to expansion, while mid-sized companies must build their capabilities to lead high-value industries.
"Start-ups must be given a complete pathway, from ideas to seed capital and scaling up.
"Meanwhile, mid-sized companies must quickly become self-sustaining to lead high-value industries," he said when tabling the 2027 budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.

Sime Darby Property Bhd, the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) and the Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) have established the RM1.25 billion New Economy Venture Fund to develop data centres and logistics assets in Elmina, Selangor.

Khazanah and KWAP have also invested RM1.2 billion to help local semiconductor companies move into higher-value segments, including through a collaboration between Khazanah and the Selangor state government to develop the semiconductor industry.
To support these objectives, Khazanah Nasional Bhd's Jelawang Capital and the Retirement Fund Inc. (KWAP)'s Dana Perintis will invest RM450 million in developing start-ups.

The government will also channel RM2.1 billion through the New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP) Fund, KWAP's Dana Pemacu and Khazanah's Dana MTC to strengthen mid-sized companies in electrical and electronics, digital technology, aerospace and medical devices.

Separately, RM270 million will be provided to attract private capital through equity crowdfunding (ECF) and peer-to-peer financing platforms to support small and medium enterprises, mid-sized companies and social enterprises.
Income tax exemptions for individual investors using ECF platforms and angel investors financing early-stage technology start-ups will be extended until Dec 31, 2030.
Anwar said RM41 million would be allocated to Cradle Fund to implement the Startup Ecosystem Roadmap and provide prototype development and commercialisation grants.
The SemiconStart programme by the Malaysian Technology Development Corporation will also provide follow-on equity investments to start-ups in integrated circuit design and advanced packaging.
62e05b7af4b5bdab: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia recorded RM132 billion in investments in the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) from 2025 to June 2026, with its master plan and blueprint set to be launched by the end of this year.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who was tabling the 2027 Budget at the Dewan Rakyat today, said he would launch the plan with Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong.
Anwar said Sedenak Nexus in the northern part of the JS-SEZ had the potential to attract RM12 billion in investments and create 45,000 jobs.
He said the government would continue strengthening its special border economic zones, with trade along the Bukit Kayu Hitam-Sadao corridor reaching RM27 billion in the first six months of this year.
Among the initiatives was the development of the 49.37 hectare NCT InnoSphere as a heavy vehicle, engineering, maintenance and logistics hub serving industries in Kulim and Penang.

Anwar said Malaysia and Indonesia had also agreed to expedite the reopening of the Tebedu-Entikong trade route, while road infrastructure along the Sabah, Sarawak and Kalimantan borders would be upgraded to facilitate cross-border movement.

On the energy sector, he said Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) investment expansion in Canada LNG Phase 2, petroleum discoveries in Suriname and cooperation involving the Galkynysh gas field in Turkmenistan would strengthen Malaysia's position in the international energy supply chain.
He said Petronas's full ownership of the Pengerang Integrated Complex would strengthen its role as a strategic national asset and support fuel supply security amid global market uncertainties.

The development of the Pengerang biorefinery through partnerships with Eni's EniLive and Euglena would also expand the production of lower-carbon fuels, including sustainable aviation fuel, hydrotreated vegetable oil and bio-naphtha.

Meanwhile, Petronas and Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) participation in the Asean Power Grid initiative would strengthen regional energy security and connectivity while creating new economic opportunities.
d6d818a3052d3890: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will increase the Ecological Fiscal Transfer (EFT) fund to RM270 million under 2027 Budget, up from RM250 million allocated in 2026, to support states in conserving the country's natural heritage.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the increased allocation was aimed at encouraging community-based economic activities and ecotourism while strengthening environmental conservation efforts.
The RM20 million increase represents an 8 per cent rise from the previous year's allocation.

The EFT fund provides financial incentives to state governments to protect biodiversity and conserve forests and other ecologically important areas. The allocation has risen from RM150 million in 2023 to RM200 million in 2024, before reaching RM250 million in 2025 and remaining at that level in 2026.

"The latest increase is expected to further support state-level conservation efforts while creating opportunities for local communities to benefit from nature-based tourism and sustainable economic activities," said Anwar.
c1ef7b35a7c897de: GENEVA, Oct 9 — Virtually all of Gaza’s two million population will go through winter without adequate shelter as the Palestinian territory enters a fourth year under heavy Israeli war restrictions, the United Nations said today.
The International Organisation for Migration (IOM) said nearly 1.8 million people in the territory “are facing a fourth winter without adequate protection from rain, flooding and cold”.
The UN agency called for international funding for humanitarian aid and for Israel to ease the “constraints” on the entry of critical supplies.
A ceasefire in the Gaza war, sparked by the Hamas attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023, was announced in October last year but conditions remain dire in Gaza, according to aid agencies.
More than half of all the tents and makeshift shelters are in poor condition and should be replaced, the IOM said.
“With few alternatives available, many families are living in war-damaged buildings that pose serious risks to life.”
IOM highlighted the deaths of 21 people, including 12 children, when a war-damaged six storey building collapsed in Gaza city last month.
“Shelter materials must enter quickly, predictably and at the scale required,” said Amy Pope, the IOM director general.

The agency said the El Nino weather phenomenon risked making this year’s winter rains more intense for Gaza which “could further weaken unsafe buildings, while heavily damaged drainage systems leave communities exposed to flooding”.
Pope said the current humanitarian supplies of shelters would only cover 17 per cent of Gaza’s “identified winter needs”.
IOM added that many tents, shelter kits, wood, tools and other material positioned outside the Palestinian territory were blocked from entering.
“Approximately 8,600 IOM emergency shelter kits are pre-positioned outside Gaza and ready for delivery but continue to be turned away at crossing points by the Israeli authorities,” the agency said.

The World Health Organisation had already warned in September that Gaza faces a new health crisis with the start of the rainy season that brings an increased risk from mosquitoes and the spread of disease.

Israel has faced increased international criticism over conditions in Gaza and the entry of humanitarian aid, but has said it is preventing the entry of items that could have military use as it accuses the Hamas militant group of plotting new attacks. — AFP
242e378fb8f70b6e: KUALA LUMPUR: New companies under the Global Services Hub (GSH) incentive will enjoy a special five per cent tax rate on income from GSH activities from Jan 1, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
When tabling the 2027 Budget, he said the government would also offer a five per cent tax rate on income exceeding the baseline income of existing Principal Hub or GSH companies.
"The GSH incentive period would be extended in five-year increments, up to a maximum of 30 years," he said.
Anwar said GSH companies managing treasury and fund activities would also be exempted from withholding tax on interest payments and stamp duty on intercompany loan agreements.
The exemptions would also apply to such activities under the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) package.
He said the measures were part of efforts to make it easier for global companies to operate in Malaysia and attract highly skilled talent.
Anwar said existing DE Rantau Nomad Pass holders who had reached the two-year limit would be allowed to stay and work remotely in Malaysia for an additional two years, subject to conditions.
Meanwhile, beginning next year, spouses of expatriates holding Category I Employment Passes and Dependent Passes would also be allowed to work in Malaysia, subject to stipulated conditions.
He said the move was aimed at keeping Malaysia attractive to global talent without requiring their spouses to sacrifice their careers.
Anwar also announced the introduction of MyABE status to help Malaysian companies expand across Asean.

"The Securities Commission, in collaboration with TalentCorp, would facilitate preliminary Employment Pass applications for listed MyABE companies, with a target processing time of five working days," he said.
He said the government was reviewing the Reinvestment Allowance, including its eligibility criteria and incentive structure, to make it more targeted and improve industrial competitiveness.

In addition, the Securities Commission and Hong Kong regulators would cooperate to facilitate dual listings by Malaysian companies in both markets, with matching grants available to cover listing costs.
Anwar said the Madani government's reforms had helped restore investor confidence, with Malaysia rising to 15th place in the World Competitiveness Index in two years.
He also cited Malaysia's ranking as the top destination for digital nomads in the Rumavi Global Relocation Index 2026.
70d05279084503dc: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will provide an additional 100,000 free artificial intelligence (AI) subscriptions, expanding access to new AI applications, including ChatGPT, under the 2027 Budget.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the initiative would be expanded following an encouraging response to the existing free AI subscription programme for young people.

"Following the encouraging response to free AI subscriptions for young people, I am pleased to announce that this initiative will be strengthened with an additional 100,000 free AI subscriptions, and expanded to include new AI applications such as ChatGPT," he said.
Tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said the government would develop a sovereign AI cloud to keep Malaysians' data and the country's strategic information under national control.
He said the government continued to emphasise the importance of young people mastering future-oriented fields, including coding, data science and quantum technology.
The government would allocate RM6 billion to intensify research, development and commercialisation activities across ministries.
Meanwhile, AI Malaysia Bhd will receive nearly RM15 million to strengthen the safe and ethical AI ecosystem, supporting the target of developing 200,000 skilled AI workers.
Malaysian Digital Economy Corp will allocate RM30 million to help 4,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) adopt AI and automate their operations.
The programme will also train and certify 5,000 AI professionals.

Anwar said the Digital Rakyat platform offered free access to more than 16,000 courses and professional certificate programmes through a collaboration with Coursera, involving leading universities and industry organisations worldwide.
"Malaysia is now recognised at the highest level, Tier 1, for its readiness to transition to post-quantum cryptography.

"The National Cyber Security Agency and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission will develop local data protection technologies capable of addressing threats posed by quantum computers, while strengthening the capabilities of CSCDC Bhd," Anwar said.
MyDigital ID recorded more than 14 million registered users accessing 203 public and private sector services, enabling Malaysians to conduct transactions securely, he added.
e708a5dfded9b406: CRISIS! The ancient computer in the basement – which has something to do with our waste water system – has stopped. And while we may not know exactly what it does when it's running, we definitely know what happens when it stops. The PFY and I took a look, and while (in theory) it's possible that we could fire up a replacement machine, I can pretty much guarantee the two ISA cards, identified only by the markings "#1" and "#2", will cause a problem. This is definitely one of those situations where the buck stops elsewhere... ... "What does it mean?" the Boss asks. "It means that by tomorrow evening – if you're parking in the basement – you'll want waterproof shoes, and by the following evening, a pair of waders." "And an incinerator to burn your shoes in," the PFY adds. "So what should I do?" the Boss whines. "In your situation, I'd probably pass problem up the food chain..." I suggest. ... And up the food chain it goes, like a newspaper-wrapped turd pass-the-parcel game, going from the Boss to the Director, to the Head of HR, who buckpasses it to the CEO, who in turn farms it off to the Board for a committee decision. ... The next day I notice an unpleasantly familiar aroma in the fresh air feed to the lower floors of the building. A smell which will only get worse in the next day or two as if creeps up the building... On getting to the office, I note a couple of old blokes at reception having a quiet word with the Boss. Moments later, he calls me over. "Simon, this is, uh, Frank, and uh, Brian. They're IT troubleshooters, here to look at that machine, in the basement..." By the look of Frank and Brian I suspect the majority of their troubleshooting was done with a musket and their first job was likely switching computer time from BC to AD. They're wearing '90s band T-shirts under their sports jackets - no doubt in an effort to offset the "geriatric" vibe. In reality, though, the vibe they're actually putting off is less hipster and more hip replacement... "They just want to go take a look," the Boss says. "Do you have the keys?" A quarter hour later they're back, chatting to the Boss again. "So what did 'Age Against the Machine' and 'Clinically Deaf Leppard' have to say?" I ask, when the Boss pops into Mission Control a few minutes later. "They said the PC is totally shot," the Boss admits. "Well, glad we got some experts in," I reply. We're interrupted by the arrival of Simon and Oldfunkle. "We don't really think you need the PC," Frank says. "The sump is just a standard float tree arrangement with a couple of variable-speed pumps," Frank explains. "Variable speed MACERATING pumps," Brian adds. "Yeah," Frank continues. "So the PC was just sensing the levels and switching the pumps on. We can do all that with a bog-standard pump controller. It could be wirelessly networked to raise a high and low level alarms as well as signal pump failures. We'll probably need to pull the small sub-board out and install a new board with a couple of VFDs in it." Well color me surprised! I was planning to ask them when lock-up at their care-home is, but I'm starting to feel like I might be in the presence of actual experts... "That sounds... expensive?" the Boss asks. "Yeah, but it's surprising how much money people are willing to spend when they're knee deep in sewerage," Brian observes. "Well... uh... can you walk me through the plan. And maybe while we're at it you can fill in the Job Safety Analysis form, the Insurance Liability forms and a personal safety waiver?" The Boss and Shawl and Oats disappear back down to the basement, and within 15 minutes they're back, only without the Boss. "How's that JSA going?" I ask. "Oh, your Boss is going to stay downstairs till it's done," Frank replies. "I seriously doubt that," I counter, knowing the Boss hates filling in paperwork almost as much as he hates accountability. "Oh, I think he will," Brian says, holding up a pair of doorhandles. "So... you've locked him in the room with the sump. The very room that will be the first to experience the overflow?" "Yes. We thought that would motivate him to streamline the paperwork." "Well, you know what my assistant and I are obliged to do?" I sigh. "What's that?" Frank asks. "Pop up to the 6th floor and start flushing toilets." the PFY replies. "We should have that paperwork back within half an hour." "We may need to pop it in the incinerator by that stage," Brian observes. "Sounds like a plan!" I chip in. Always a pleasure to deal with a professional. d73bacae50375cfc: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will defer National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) loan repayments next year for borrowers earning RM2,500 or less a month, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced when ta2027 Budget: PTPTN repayments deferred for low-income borrowersbling the 2027 Budget.
Borrowers earning between RM2,500 and RM3,000 a month will be required to make minimum monthly repayments of RM50, he said.
The measure is expected to benefit more than 400,000 PTPTN borrowers.
Anwar said students must also have access to food assistance.
The Dapur Siswa Madani programme will be expanded to polytechnics and teacher education institutes, with an allocation of RM20 million.
The initiative will provide cooking equipment, food supplies and meals under the Menu Kasih Siswa programme at RM5 per meal, he said.

Anwar also announced that flight ticket assistance under the FlySiswa Madani 2027 programme would be increased to RM500 from RM400, benefiting more than 60,000 students at public higher education institutions.
a62f0a0f97d1b81d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Health Ministry will receive RM47.7 billion next year, up from this year’s RM46.5 billion, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
While tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said RM1.2 billion will be distributed for repair, upgrade and maintenance works of all public hospitals and clinics.
A total of nine new facilities, including a specialist clinic complex and daycare treatment centre at Hospital Sultanah Aminah in Johor, will also be constructed next year, Anwar said.
“More than RM770 million will also be allocated for the procurement of modern and sophisticated equipment to speed up diagnosis and treatment,” Anwar said.

The new assets, he said, would include haemodialysis facilities in hospitals nationwide, 400 new government ambulances, a specialist hospital under Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) with robotic surgery expertise as well as clinical simulation equipment and science laboratories in 18 training institutes.
Anwar also announced a RM200 million allocation for outsourcing of patients to other hospitals to reduce waiting period.
6ef686ab274cc3d2: KUALA LUMPUR: Micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) applying for halal certification for the first time will receive a matching grant of up to RM5,000.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that many local entrepreneurs have quality products but face challenges obtaining halal certification and accessing wider markets.

"The government has agreed to provide matching grants of up to RM5,000 to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) seeking halal certification for the first time," he said when tabling the 2027 Budget at the Dewan Rakyat here today.
Anwar added that grants of RM25,000 will also be provided to strengthen halal MSMEs in sectors such as cosmetics and pharmaceuticals.
62689998d1604e14: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — School repair allocation is set to be doubled to RM2 billion next year.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling the Budget 2027 in Parliament, said the allocation increase would cover different types of schools, including national schools, Chinese and Tamil national-type schools, as well as registered religious schools, tahfiz institutions and pondok schools.
“The allocation for national schools will increase to RM900 million, while Chinese national-type schools will receive RM100 million and Tamil national-type schools, RM50 million.

“Registered religious schools, tahfiz institutions and pondok schools under the Islamic Development Department of Malaysia (Jakim) will receive RM200 million, with the scope of funding expanded to cover their operating costs.
“The government recognises the urgent need to improve infrastructure at Tamil national-type schools despite their relatively smaller enrolment,” Anwar told Parliament today.
Separately, nearly RM1.3 billion will be allocated to upgrade 682 dilapidated schools, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak.
These allocations are part of the Education Ministry’s huge allocation of RM69 billion under the Budget 2027, up from RM66.2 billion this year.

“To accommodate an expected 500,000 pupils entering Year One next year, including more than 70,000 aged six, the government expects to complete 3,500 additional classrooms by the end of this year using the Industrialised Building System (IBS),” Anwar added.

The Prime Minister also announced plans for new schools, preschool buildings and additional facilities at existing schools, including SK Seri Chemor in Ipoh, Perak; Kompleks Sekolah Bandar Serenia in Sepang, Selangor; and a replacement building for SJK (Tamil) Ladang Pamol in Kluang, Johor.
Other projects include SJK (C) Bandar Mahkota Cheras and a preschool building at SK Bulu Silou in Keningau, Sabah.
A new matriculation college is also being built in Marang, Terengganu.

f0fd2b6b72535d72: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will extend green tax incentives until the end of 2030, offering up to 100 per cent investment tax allowances for green projects and electric vehicle charging stations.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said companies purchasing green technology assets for their own use will also qualify for investment tax allowances of up to 100 per cent.
He announced these measures when tabling the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar said Malaysia must intensify its energy transition agenda to ensure a sustainable energy supply, despite the country having weathered the impact of the Middle East conflict.
"However, the energy transition agenda must be intensified to ensure the country's energy supply sustainability in the long term," he said.
As part of efforts to strengthen electricity infrastructure, Tenaga Nasional Bhd will invest RM15 billion to reinforce the national grid and ensure it can meet growing electricity demand.
UEM Lestra will invest RM1 billion, including in an energy storage project at Kuala Lumpur International Airport and a one-gigawatt hybrid energy project in Johor.
Meanwhile, the RM1 billion KWAP Climate Fund will be channelled into green projects, including renewable energy and decarbonisation initiatives.
4c58f01bedad0cc1: KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists who cause accidents while driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs will be required to compensate their victims under a proposed amendment to the Road Transport Act.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would amend the law to make compensation mandatory for victims of accidents involving drunk or drug-impaired drivers.

Announcing the measure when tabling the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said road accidents involving drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs remained a concern despite stricter enforcement.
He cited a fatal accident along the East Coast Expressway Phase 1 (LPT1) in Temerloh on the eve of National Day, which claimed four lives, including those of a husband, wife and their young child.
"As of August this year, 28 fatal cases involving drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs were recorded.
"Such tragedies are a wake-up call to us that despite stricter enforcement, violations of road regulations remain a concern.
"Therefore, as a tougher measure, the government will amend the Road Transport Act to make it mandatory for drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs to pay compensation to victims," he said.
Anwar, who is also the finance minister, did not specify when the amendment would be tabled in Parliament or how the compensation mechanism would be implemented.
In a separate measure to improve road safety, Anwar announced that commercial vehicles would be required to install telematics systems to monitor speed, location and risky driving behaviour.

"Telematics systems will be made mandatory in commercial vehicles to monitor speed, location and risky driving patterns, including linking them to alcohol detection devices before drivers begin their journeys," he said.
Anwar said the installation would remain voluntary until 2027, while the government develops a driver database to strengthen enforcement.
The Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) will also provide health screening vouchers for commercial vehicle drivers to identify medical conditions that could affect their ability to drive safely.
5e4d0f4914af9299: KUALA LUMPUR: Private hospitals will be required to adopt standardised billing categories from 2027 to help patients better understand their medical expenses.

"From 2027, private hospital bills will use uniform and transparent categories of charges so that patients understand each payment and price distortions can be reduced," said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the government would also expand electronic medical records based on the principle of "one individual, one record".
He said the measures were aimed at improving transparency in private healthcare costs and ensuring patients had a clearer understanding of the charges imposed on them.
Meanwhile, the government will develop the e-CKAPS portal to enable private healthcare facilities to complete licensing procedures entirely online from 2027.

"The e-CKAPS portal will also be developed to enable licensing procedures for private healthcare facilities to be conducted entirely online from 2027, with processing times targeted to be reduced by up to 65 per cent," he said.
71cb2b8edfae41a5: KUALA LUMPUR: Comedian and radio presenter Jep Sepahtu has attracted attention after sharing receipts documenting his business zakat payments, including a payment of RM300,000 in 2025.
Jep, whose real name is Mohd Nadzri Zainal Abidin, 41, said he shared the receipts as proof that he had fulfilled his religious obligation, rather than to boast about the amounts paid.
"Anyone can talk. Especially nowadays, in the podcast era, all you need is a mouth to talk," he said in a social media post on yesterday.
He added that the income he received was a divine blessing and that he believed in sharing his good fortune with others.
"How could I possibly take what belongs to other people?" he said, emphasising that he had no intention of withholding what was rightfully due to others.
The receipts reportedly documented his business zakat payments from 2016 to 2025, with the amounts varying over the years and reaching RM300,000 in the latest records shared.
Jep also expressed appreciation to Astro for giving him opportunities through Sepahtu Reunion and Sinar between 2015 and 2025, acknowledging the role the broadcaster played in his career.
His post came amid renewed attention surrounding tensions involving fellow comedian Shuib and discussions about friendship, payments and the distribution of earnings.
Jep had previously voiced his frustration over the matter and urged others not to exploit such issues for publicity.
By making the receipts public, Jep appeared keen to address questions about his financial responsibilities and reinforce his belief that zakat is an obligation.
He maintained that the money he earned was a blessing and that sharing it with those entitled to receive it was part of his responsibility.
ecb97cd20b183c39: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Existing road transport law will be amended to make it mandatory for motorists driving under the influence to pay compensation to victims.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the amendments would cover driving under the influence of both alcohol and drugs under the Road Transport Act.

Four people, including three family members, were killed and three others injured in a collision involving 11 vehicles at KM110.4 of the LPT1, near the Temerloh Toll Plaza exit in Lanchang, Temerloh, at about 10 pm on August 31.
Citing the crash, Anwar said such tragedies were deeply distressing and showed that road safety violations remained a concern despite tighter enforcement.
“As of August, 28 fatal cases involving drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs had been recorded.
“Therefore, as a sterner measure, the government will amend the Road Transport Act,” he said while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today.

Anwar also said a telematics system will be made compulsory for installation on commercial vehicles to monitor speed, location and risky driving patterns, including links to alcohol detection devices to check drivers before they begin their journeys.
“Voluntary implementation will continue until 2027 while the government develops a database of drivers for enforcement purposes,” he said.
He also said the Social Security Organisation (Socso) will provide health screening vouchers for commercial vehicle drivers to detect medical risks that could affect their ability to drive safely.
385b44fc83fed1ae: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The federal government today announced an increase in allocations for the maintenance of Chinese New Villages and non-Muslim houses of worship from 2027 onwards.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the allocation for infrastructure upgrades in Chinese New Villages will be increased to more than RM100 million, including repairs and rebuilding of ageing facilities.
“Meanwhile, funding for the maintenance of registered non-Muslim houses of worship will also be increased to RM80 million,” he said during the tabling of Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat here today.
Separately, Anwar said the ongoing Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani initiatives have benefitted nearly 500 villages and 1,700 schools nationwide since 2024.
Therefore, the government will introduce the Komuniti Angkat Madani initiative with an allocation of RM50 million for 2027, focusing on helping urban People’s Housing Project (PPR) communities.

“For example, the Attorney General’s Chambers provided facilities in Kampung Jilid 8 in Kuala Muda, Kedah, including a football field, a fishermen’s jetty and a Bank Simpanan Nasional ATM, which also benefit residents of neighbouring villages.
“Meanwhile, SK Telok Kalong in Terengganu received a comfortable special remedial classroom and robotics learning facilities for pupils through contributions from Sime Darby Berhad,” he said.
He then expressed his appreciation to the management of ministries, departments and agencies, as well as corporate bodies, for contributing to the initiatives.
8aeccfa7b8c0a941: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government expects to spend more than RM80 billion on subsidies, assistance and incentives next year.

Tabling Budget 2027 in Parliament, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said fuel subsidies were expected to remain high at RM40 billion, while assistance through the Social Welfare Department would amount to nearly RM3.3 billion.
“The government will also increase the allocation for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to RM16 billion next year, up from RM15 billion this year.
“All STR recipients would receive SARA assistance of up to RM150 a month, or RM1,800 annually, benefiting up to nine million recipients.
“Non-STR recipients aged 18 and above will also receive RM100 in SARA Madani credit twice next year, once before Hari Raya Aidilfitri and another ahead of the 70th anniversary of Merdeka.
“The two payments are expected to benefit up to 13 million Malaysians, including those in the middle 40 (M40) income group,” Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, told Parliament today.
The government will also expand the use of SARA credits to include fresh produce sold at 216 pasar tani (farmers’ market) and tamu (open-air markets) under Fama nationwide.
There are currently 15,000 SARA partner outlets, including 6,800 small grocery shops and cooperatives.
The government aims to increase the number of participating small grocery shops to 10,000 before the end of this year.
Separately, the allocation for Jualan Rahmah Madani and Jualan Agro Madani will rise to RM750 million from RM630 million, with 35,000 sales events targeted next year.
Of these, 30,000 Jualan Rahmah events will be held across all state constituencies, with greater emphasis on rural areas, low-cost housing areas and urban People’s Housing Project (PPR) communities.
The programme will also expand beyond conventional grocery shops to include vending machines, while Jualan Rahmah Madani Borong will help small traders.
Another 5,000 Jualan Agro Madani events will offer fresh agricultural produce, including fish, chicken, vegetables and fruits, at prices up to 30 per cent lower.

The government will also allocate RM250 million to expand the distribution of essential goods to rural and remote areas, including six new locations such as Kampung Terian in Penampang, Sabah, and Kampung Dato’ Godam in Pusa, Sarawak.
c87b5af63664147e: KUALA LUMPUR: Households will receive rebates of up to RM200 for energy-efficient air conditioners and refrigerators under the Nur Madani programme.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said hotter weather contributed to higher electricity consumption, highlighting the need to encourage more efficient energy use.
The initiative is part of the government's broader push to promote green technology adoption and manage rising electricity demand.

Separately, the government will extend green investment tax incentives until Dec 31, 2030, including investment tax allowances of up to 100 per cent for qualifying green technology projects, electric vehicle charging stations and green technology assets acquired for own use.
The incentives aim to encourage private sector investment in green technology and accelerate the adoption of sustainable energy solutions.
21986837ebe2da40: SHANGHAI: Top seed Alexander Zverev churned out an opening win over Chinese wildcard Wu Yibing 6-4, 7-6 (7/4) at the Shanghai Masters on Friday to advance into the third round.
A dive left the German grimacing and grabbing his left ankle during the 11th game of the second set, with Wu, ranked 113th in the world, going up 6-5.
But the 29-year-old held serve and forced a tie-break, capitalising on a series of errors to win on his second match point when the home hope fired long.
"Credit to him, he was playing amazing tennis," Zverev told the crowd afterwards.
"He hits every ball as hard as he can," he added in another on-court interview, crediting a reliable serve for his straight-sets win.
Zverev, the world number two, is on track to end the year with the top ranking after Jannik Sinner announced he was ending his 2026 season due to injury.
Zverev next faces Quentin Halys of France, who downed Belgium's Alexander Blockx in three sets.
Earlier, third-seeded Ben Shelton beat Germany's Daniel Altmaier 6-3, 7-6 (8/6) and will play France's Arthur Gea in the third round.
"Tough match-up," said the American, who double-faulted five times across the gritty two-hour match. "Happy with the way I finished."
It was a fitting birthday present for Shelton, who turned 24 on Friday, though he hinted he may pass on indulging, telling an on-court interviewer: "I hate cake."
Frenchman Adrian Mannarino upset sixth-seeded Flavio Cobolli 6-1, 4-6, 6-3.
Cobolli, the French Open finalist, twice fell to the ground as he failed to convert two break points in the last game.
The Italian, 24, saved a match point with a well-placed volley but could not stay afloat as 38-year-old Mannarino kept him running and forced him into a backhand he could not return.
Mannarino, ranked 83rd, will face either Karen Khachanov or Arthur Fery in the next round.
Elsewhere in the draw, Japanese qualifier Rei Sakamoto beat Russia's Andrey Rublev 6-4, 6-4.
Sakamoto, the world number 137, will next play ninth-seeded Alex de Minaur, who advanced after his opponent Alex Molcan withdrew before play.
Later on Friday, Serbian veteran Novak Djokovic was due to start his title bid in the second round against Poland's Hubert Hurkacz. - AFP
2fe7616865a699b5: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The service tax rate for elderly care services will be reduced from eight to six per cent, starting January 1, 2027.
A full exemption will also be granted on care fees up to RM96,000 a year.
Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim made the announcement while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar said the government will also increase financial aid for senior citizens to RM1.3 billion next year, benefiting nearly 200,000 recipients.
“The government will also draft a Senior Citizens Bill to tackle neglect (of the elderly) and strengthen the care ecosystem as a whole,” he said.
“More than 40 million ringgit will also be allocated to HRD Corp to train 8,000 people in the elderly care sector and open job opportunities for them,” he added.
Two National Integrated Care Centres of Excellence (NICE) will also be developed in Penang and Sarawak to support training, research and elderly care, Anwar said.

On a related development, Anwar said Employees Provident Fund (EPF) members aged 55 and 60 can opt for monthly withdrawals under i-Emas so that their remaining savings can continue generating dividends.
8caa6270b635ec36: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — All Malaysian citizens will be automatically registered as members of the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) upon turning 18 to encourage earlier retirement savings, under a measure announced in Budget 2027.
The move aims to strengthen social protection by helping Malaysians prepare for retirement from a younger age.
Currently, employees are automatically registered with the EPF when the fund receives their first employer contribution.
Individuals can also register through the EPF’s i-Akaun application.
The EPF is Malaysia’s main retirement savings fund, with contributions from employees and employers helping members build savings for their later years.
3403b21e3856b3d2: KUALA LUMPUR: Government-linked companies (GLCs) and Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) are targeting RM58 billion in procurement from Bumiputera companies as the government steps up efforts to expand their participation in the economy.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said GLC procurement guidelines, which have not been reviewed since 2006, would be updated from 2027, with vendor performance assessed based on business growth, innovation and access to new markets.

Tabling the 2027 Budget at the Dewan Rakyat here today, he said the government would increase procurement allocated to Bumiputera contractors in grades G1 to G4 to RM7.5 billion next year, from RM4 billion this year.

The government would also strengthen financing and investment support for Bumiputera businesses, with Perbadanan Usahawan Nasional Bhd's financing increased to RM500 million from RM350 million, while Bumiputera Agenda Steering Unit (Teraju) would provide up to RM1 billion in financing.

Government-linked investment companies (GLICs) will invest RM2 billion to empower Bumiputera companies, including helping them prepare for public listings and strengthen ownership of strategic properties.
Khazanah Nasional Bhd and Teraju will also establish the RM250 million Dana Ciptawan to support the growth of Bumiputera mid-sized companies.

The government will increase the direct appointment procurement limit for maintenance, repairs and improvements to government facilities to RM200,000, while raising the quotation limit to RM3 million.
To expand Bumiputera participation in renewable energy, RM1.5 billion will be channelled into developing centralised solar parks for government buildings.
Under the large scale solar 6 (LSS6) programme, 150 megawatts would be allocated to Bumiputera companies to support their participation in the clean energy industry.
The 10 Juara Bumiputera programme would continue with an allocation of RM40 million to develop 15 promising companies by 2027.
The government would also provide a new strategic land endowment worth RM1 billion, covering 50 acres in Kuala Lumpur, to Yayasan Pelaburan Bumiputra.
Anwar said the land was intended for development by Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB), taking into account affordable housing needs and Bumiputera interests.
The government will provide matching grants of up to RM5,000 to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) seeking halal certification for the first time.
Grants of RM25,000 will be available to strengthen halal businesses in sectors such as cosmetics and pharmaceuticals.
f9b96059a26ac0b9: KUALA LUMPUR: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) will benefit from a one percentage point reduction in income tax rates, as the government moves to ease rising operating costs and support business cash flow.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling 2027 Budget in Dewan Rakyat today, said the tax rate for the first RM150,000 of chargeable income will be reduced to 14 per cent.
Anwar said the tax rate for chargeable income between RM150,000 and RM600,000 will be reduced to 16 per cent.
"This will provide additional income of up to RM6,000 to 300,000 to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs)," he said.
The government was also proposing several other tax measures to support businesses and improve productivity.
Anwar noted that the value threshold for each small asset eligible for capital allowance will be increased to RM3,000.
"For companies other than MSMEs, the overall claim limit will be raised to RM30,000," he said.
In addition, Anwar said manufacturers would also be allowed to claim back sales tax paid on machinery, spare parts and equipment purchased from local traders or distributors.

To improve the productivity of local companies, he said the accelerated capital allowance for expenditure on locally sourced plant and machinery, as well as information and communications technology (ICT) equipment and software, will be extended until December 31, 2030.

Anwar said the government also proposed a lower stamp duty of RM10 for agreements involving the utilisation of excess credit facilities provided by banks to mid-tier companies, completed between Jan 1, 2027 and Dec 31, 2030.
Similarly, he said peer-to-peer (P2P) financing loan agreements executed through financing platforms during the same period would be subject to a stamp duty of only RM10.
"Full stamp duty exemption will be granted for the opening of savings and current accounts from January 1, 2027," he added.

f5b74fc6e6dd16c6: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will launch the MediAsas health plan in January 2027, offering affordable premiums and more predictable hospital charges.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said hospital charges under the plan would be based on the diagnosis and treatment required, allowing costs to be better controlled and anticipated.
"Employees Provident Fund (EPF) members aged below 55 would be allowed to pay their MediAsas premiums using savings from Account Sejahtera, he said.

"The government will also subsidise the first-year premium by RM200 per employee for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) with fewer than 75 employees, capped at 50 employees per company," he said when tabling the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat.
He said the initiative was expected to benefit up to 200,000 workers.
c8504d59b5293f61: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will increase the value of government procurement allocated to Bumiputera contractors in grades G1 to G4 to RM7.5 billion under 2027 Budget, up from RM4 billion this year.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the move is aimed at addressing concerns raised by Bumiputera contractors and strengthening their business capacity.

"For government facility maintenance, repairs and upgrading works, the limit for direct appointments will be raised to RM200,000, while quotation-based procurement will be allowed for projects worth up to RM3 million," he said.
Anwar said the measures followed engagement sessions with representatives of Bumiputera contractors' associations and companies to better understand the challenges facing their businesses.
"Teraju will also provide financing of up to RM1 billion and have its capacity strengthened to monitor 32 Bumiputera projects more effectively across government departments, agencies and companies.
"Meanwhile, financing funds provided by Perbadanan Usahawan Nasional Bhd (PUNB) will increase to RM500 million from RM350 million," he said.
The government will introduce a stamp duty concession of RM10 for loan and financing agreements under the Cakna II scheme, which will run from Jan 1, 2027, to Dec 31, 2030.
The same concession under Cakna I will also be extended until Dec 31, 2030.
Government-linked companies (GLCs) and Petronas are targeting RM58 billion in procurement from Bumiputera companies.
Starting in 2027, GLC procurement guidelines, which have not been revised since 2006, will be updated.
The success of vendors will also be assessed based on business growth, innovation and their ability to penetrate new markets.
Anwar said government-linked investment companies (GLICs) would invest RM2 billion to strengthen Bumiputera companies.
For example, Ekuinas and PHB will help Bumiputera companies prepare for public listings and strengthen strategic property ownership.
Khazanah Nasional and Teraju will also establish the RM250 million Ciptawan Fund to support the growth of mid-sized Bumiputera companies.
The government will develop centralised solar parks for government buildings through an investment of RM1.5 billion.
The initiative is expected to create opportunities for 33 Bumiputera companies in construction, engineering and maintenance.
Under the Large Scale Solar 6 (LSS6) programme, Anwar said 150 megawatts of capacity will be allocated to Bumiputera companies to help them expand their participation in the clean energy industry.
"The 10 Juara Bumiputera programme will also continue, with an allocation of RM40 million to develop 15 promising companies by 2027.

"The measures form part of the government's efforts to expand Bumiputera participation in government procurement, strengthen business financing and create opportunities in strategic industries," he said.

57b3e85aef551bd4: KUALA LUMPUR: Sabah and Sarawak remain the largest recipients of federal allocations under the 2027 Budget, with Sabah receiving RM18.7 billion and Sarawak RM16.2 billion to support infrastructure development, electricity supply and education.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling the 2027 Budget today, said the government would increase the number of Public Service Department (PSD) scholarships for students from both states.
"This means 4,200 children from Sabah and Sarawak will have the opportunity to pursue higher education each year," he said.
Meanwhile, the federal government will begin formal negotiations to develop the Sibu Special Economic Zone (SEZ) for Sarawak.

Anwar said the Sarawak government had expressed its commitment to developing the zone, with negotiations to focus on finalising the incentive framework, a one-stop investment facilitation centre and strategic infrastructure requirements.
"The federal government will begin formal negotiations to finalise the incentive framework, a one-stop investment facilitation centre and strategic infrastructure requirements," he said.
The government has also agreed to install the STATCOM system at the Dam Road and Segaliud Main Intake Substations in Sabah at RM204 million.
The Southern Link Transmission Line project will continue as a long-term measure to ensure a reliable electricity supply in Sabah.
Under the Budget, road projects in Sabah and Sarawak will receive RM3.3 billion.
"Among them, the Trans Borneo Highway SST for the Miri section has been issued, while the Limbang and Lawas sections are expected by the end of this year.
"Sarawak-Sabah Link Road 1 and Pan Borneo Sabah Phase 1B are targeted for completion by the end of next year.
He said RM350 million had been set aside for G1 to G4 contractors to maintain federal roads in Sabah and Sarawak.

e151bebdd479a51c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will be allocated RM400 million to create 120 acres of new green spaces and upgrade public facilities as part of efforts to make the capital more liveable.

During the tabling of Budget 2027 today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the plans include a 22km of covered pedestrian walkways linking landmarks such as the National Mosque, Dataran Merdeka and Central Market, as well as connecting public housing to schools, clinics and transport hubs.

A 100-acre leasehold site in Bukit Kiara is also being gazetted as a federal park, while buggy services are to be introduced for visitors, particularly elderly travellers, heading to destinations such as the National Monument, Botanical Gardens and Carcosa Seri Negara.

Anwar also commended Khazanah Nasional’s Warisan KL initiative, which has drawn 500,000 visitors following the restoration of the Sultan Abdul Samad Building. The next phase of conservation will focus on Dayabumi Tower, Kuala Lumpur Railway Station and the KTMB headquarters.
Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) was recognised for restoring Merdeka Stadium, with the National Stadium next in line.
Anwar said entertainment duty will be exempted for arts, cultural and sporting events at both venues to encourage greater use.
He added that two DBKL buildings, the Anjung Kelana Homeless Transformation Centre in Taman Desa and the Cheras Temporary Market, will be upgraded into day centres for senior citizens.
321218a1900908f5: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has announced housing initiatives under 2027 Budget, including nearly RM1 billion in funding for affordable housing programmes and stamp duty exemptions for first-time homebuyers.
He said Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil would be developed as a residential community with facilities including a vertical school.
Registration for its first phase will open on Monday, he said.
The government will allocate nearly RM1 billion for housing initiatives, including the Rumah Mesra Rakyat scheme and Program Residensi Rakyat.
Four new housing projects are also planned in Kulai, Johor; Nilai, Negeri Sembilan; Paya Rumput, Melaka; and Lembah Pertang, Terengganu.
The government will also provide housing financing guarantees of up to RM20 billion through Syarikat Jaminan Kredit Perumahan (SJKP).

Anwar said the initiative was expected to benefit 80,000 first-time homebuyers, particularly self-employed people who may struggle to secure housing loans because they do not have a fixed monthly income.
First-time homebuyers purchasing properties priced at RM500,000 or below will receive a full stamp duty exemption on loan agreements and property transfer instruments, he said.
For properties priced at up to RM750,000, a full exemption will apply to the first RM500,000, while a 50 per cent exemption will cover the remaining amount.
The exemptions will apply to sale and purchase agreements completed between Jan 1, 2027 and Dec 31, 2030.

To help achieve the target of zero abandoned housing projects by 2030, the government will also introduce a full stamp duty exemption on loan agreements and property transfer instruments involving rescue contractors or developers and the original homebuyers.
Anwar said this exemption would also apply from Jan 1, 2027 to Dec 31, 2030.
7b66fe7832294f9f: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur's iconic railway station, famed for its striking Moorish-Islamic architecture and white domes, is set to become the next landmark in the capital's heritage revival, with Khazanah Nasional Bhd expanding its conservation efforts to three historic buildings.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Kuala Lumpur Railway Station (KTM Station), Dayabumi Complex and Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) headquarters (HQ) would be the next focus of the national investment fund's conservation initiative.

Anwar announced the plans in his 2027 Budget speech here today, highlighting the potential of heritage restoration to revitalise Kuala Lumpur's historic core, build cultural tourism and reconnect the public with the city's architectural legacy.
Together, the three buildings offer a snapshot of Kuala Lumpur's evolution, from the railway-led growth of the colonial era to the architectural ambitions of modern Malaysia.
The conservation effort is intended to preserve their historical and architectural significance while exploring how these landmarks can remain relevant and accessible to the public.

The initiative also reinforces the role of heritage assets in shaping Kuala Lumpur's urban identity, with restored landmarks offering opportunities to attract visitors, support surrounding businesses and strengthen the appeal of the city's historic core.

The railway station, completed in 1910, is among the capital's most recognisable landmarks. Designed by British architect Arthur Benison Hubback, it features horseshoe arches, domes and ornate detailing inspired by Moorish and Islamic architecture.

Standing along Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin, the station has witnessed Kuala Lumpur's transformation from a tin-mining settlement into a modern capital, while serving generations of rail passengers travelling along Peninsular Malaysia's north-south network.

Its neighbouring former KTMB headquarters, completed in 1917, forms part of the city's historic railway precinct, reflecting the development of the country's railway infrastructure and architectural identity during the early 20th century.
The planned conservation marks another step in Khazanah's KL Heritage initiative, following restoration works at the Sultan Abdul Samad Building and its surrounding precinct.

In his 2027 Budget speech, Anwar commended the initiative's impact, noting that the restored Sultan Abdul Samad Building had attracted more than 500,000 local and international visitors since the project's completion.
The increase in visitors has helped breathe new life into the historic city centre, supporting cultural tourism and creating opportunities for businesses around the heritage precinct.
The next phase will extend this approach to landmarks representing different stages of Kuala Lumpur's development.

Completed in 1984, Dayabumi was a defining milestone in Malaysia's post-independence architecture, combining modern high-rise design with Islamic geometric motifs. Its distinctive form reflects the country's effort to incorporate cultural identity into an increasingly modern urban landscape.
b2f97dc9cf28bd0f: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 demonstrates how unity among its multiracial population remains a key strength in achieving international excellence, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.

8725241ba2bfa521: KUALA LUMPUR: First-time homebuyers purchasing properties priced up to RM500,000 will enjoy full stamp duty exemptions on loan agreements and instruments of transfer under the 2027 Budget 2027, in a move to improve housing affordability.

2d16dd966e422841: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The allocation for rural road projects will be increased to RM2.3 billion, compared to RM1.3 billion in 2022.

479166e1ce46c4bb: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government has proposed a full stamp duty exemption on loan agreements and instruments of transfer for first homes priced up to RM500,000, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.

91818c834a16b33b: SINGAPORE, Oct 9 — Air quality in the Republic is deteriorating towards the very unhealthy range, with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) in central Singapore rising to 191 by 4pm this afternoon, up from 181 at noon.
The latest reading marks a new high for 2026, surpassing the record of 181 set earlier in the day and placing air quality just 10 points away from the very unhealthy range.
At 4pm, PSI in all five regions remain in the unhealthy range, with the next highest reading of 183 recorded in western Singapore.
Readings of 201 to 300 denote the very unhealthy range.
Meanwhile, one-hour PM2.5 concentrations remained in the elevated band in all five regions.
The highest concentration reading of 148 was recorded in western Singapore, followed by 145 in central Singapore.
Concentration readings between 56 to 150µg/m3 fall within the elevated band, while readings between 151 and 250 are in the high band.

When one-hour PM2.5 concentration readings are in the high band, healthy persons should avoid strenuous outdoor activity for the next hour, while vulnerable persons should avoid all outdoor activity for the next hour.
Data from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre showed 162 hotspots in Kalimantan on Oct 8, while there were 314 hotspots detected in Sumatra.
What happens if PSI is ‘very unhealthy’?
Preschools and schools have measures in place to safeguard the wellbeing of students. This includes adjusting outdoor activities and the use of air purifiers.
According to the Ministry of Education (MOE), it will consider closing schools when the air quality forecast for the next day is in the hazardous range. This occurs when PSI exceeds 300.
Any school closure will be announced at around the same time as the daily haze situation update in the evening, and schools will inform parents accordingly.
For now, with air quality in the unhealthy range, workplace safety remains a focus, and employers are urged to reduce the duration of prolonged or strenuous work for healthy employees.
For vulnerable workers, especially the elderly and pregnant women, they should minimise prolonged or strenuous outdoor work, while those with chronic heart and lung conditions should avoid such work.
Employers should also provide suitable protective equipment, considering pollutants present in the work environment.
Members of the public should check the latest one-hour PM2.5 concentration readings before participating in outdoor activities. — AsiaOne
cbe7d6275f24eefd: LONDON, Oct 9 — Everton’s owners have put the club up for sale less than two years after acquiring a controlling interest in the club, reported PA Media/dpa.

b617fc439b014f70: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government and e-hailing platform Grab will jointly fund a RM160 million financial package under Budget 2027 to increase the net earnings of e-hailing and p-hailing workers and improve their welfare.
Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim made the announcement today while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today.

Anwar said the RM160 million package will cover the increase of minimum income for e-hailing and p-hailing drivers, maintenance and insurance of their vehicles and Social Security Organisation (Socso) contributions.
“This would mean that the net income for e-hailing drivers would rise to a median of RM227 a month and to a median of RM100 a month for p-hailing riders,” Anwar said.
He said the Gig Workers’ Consultative Council will also be finalising the minimum wage rate, income formula and a standard minimum social protection for all gig workers by early 2027.

Additionally, Anwar said the government will also offer 35 per cent matching of Socso incentives for e-hailing and p-hailing workers, which would be increased to 50 per cent if their respective platforms also pitch in.
The government, he said, will also offer matching Socso incentives up to 70 per cent for another 200 self-employed people working in 17 non-mandatory sectors.

Anwar said the government will also provide an Employees Provident Fund (EPF) matching contribution incentives up to RM600 a year of RM6,000 for life to encourage retirement savings among the e-hailing and p-hailing drivers.
Anwar also announced additional tax relief up to RM150 for voluntary Socso contributions under Skim Lindung 24 Jam dan Lindung Kendiri.
“BSN and Agrobank will also allocate RM270 million ringgit to extend funding for gig workers who want to start businesses or buy their first home,” he added.
1df7e47d400c9431: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Federal allocations to states will be determined by their respective development needs rather than distributed equally, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said during the tabling of Budget 2027 today.
Anwar said the approach was intended to bridge the gap between developed, developing and lagging states.

“This is the principle reflected in the allocation of funds to the states: enabling more developed states to continue making great strides, giving states that are still developing room to accelerate their progress, and empowering regions that have fallen behind to close the development gap,” he said.

He attributed the approach to American philosopher John Rawls, who in his 1971 book A Theory of Justice questioned whether justice should be judged solely by the greatest benefit to society or built upon arrangements genuinely fair to every individual.

“That is the meaning of equality in this context. It does not mean that everyone receives the same things, but that each state receives what is reasonable and appropriate to enable its people to progress alongside others,” he said.
4a774cb000b4159d: MELAKA, Oct 9 — The High Court here today sentenced a man to 13 years in prison after finding him guilty of causing the death of an elderly man during a robbery in April 2023.
Judge Datuk D. Suria Kumar meted out the sentence to Muhammad Faris Amjad Jamalludin, 27, after taking into account the facts of the case and the mitigating factors presented by the defence.
He also reprimanded the accused for leaving Tan Kue Seng, 71, in a dying condition in a roadside drain along Jalan Gapam in Melaka Tengah on April 9, 2023, without seeking emergency assistance.

“Your actions were inhumane. I hope you repent and find honest work to support your family. The court views seriously offences involving snatch theft and robbery that result in injury or death to victims,” he said when passing sentence.
The judge also questioned the accused’s failure to call an ambulance for the victim.

“Imagine you were riding a motorcycle and were suddenly kicked. How would you feel? You would already be helpless, in the rain, at night and in the cold. The second accused probably had a phone too, but did not call for an ambulance,” he said.
He said the accused had kicked the victim’s motorcycle forcefully with his left foot, seemingly using that limb as a weapon to injure the victim before his death.
Meanwhile, Muhammad Faris Amjad’s friend, Noorbaizura Mohd Fuad, 37, the first accused in the case, was acquitted and discharged of the same charge.
According to the facts of the case, both accused, acting with common intention, kicked the victim’s motorcycle after seeing the elderly man riding alone.
The act caused the victim’s motorcycle to veer off the road shoulder before plunging into a concrete drain.
Muhammad Faris Amjad then took the victim’s waist bag and left him dying before using the victim’s bank card to make purchases.
The victim’s body was found by his son on April 11, 2023, swollen and emitting a foul smell, in the same drain.
Muhammad Faris Amjad was charged under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code (Act 574), read together with Section 34 of the same Code, which provides for a jail term of up to 30 years and a fine.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Muhammad Azfar Mahmod appeared for the prosecution, while Tiu Leong Kim represented Muhammad Faris Amjad and Mak Kah Keong represented Noorbaizura.
The court ordered Muhammad Faris Amjad’s prison sentence to take effect from the date of his arrest, June 11, 2023. — Bernama
298137c3863a7d8c: PETALING JAYA: The government will provide 50 acres of strategic land in Kuala Lumpur, valued at RM1 billion, as a new endowment to Yayasan Pelaburan Bumiputra (YPB).

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the land would be allocated to YPB for development by Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB), taking into account the need for affordable housing and the interests of the Bumiputera community.

Anwar also said the government would increase the value of procurement allocated to Bumiputera contractors in grades G1 to G4 to RM7.5 billion under Budget 2027, up from RM4 billion this year.

28376f3528f4ada5: PETALING JAYA: As of 4pm today, 11 areas in Peninsular Malaysia recorded air pollutant index (API) readings above 180, the threshold for school closures under an education ministry order.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (Apims), Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded the highest reading at 190, followed by Seremban in Negeri Sembilan at 189.

Yesterday, education minister Fadhlina Sidek announced that all educational institutions in Selangor, Melaka, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya would close today because of the worsening haze.

5f83008d7b145483: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan bercadang memberikan pengecualian penuh duti setem bagi pembelian rumah pertama berharga sehingga RM500,000 menerusi Belanjakan 2027.

1d11a2fc933bda4c: PETALING JAYA: The government will offer matching grants of up to RM5,000 to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) seeking halal certification for the first time.

15e8cca97d95b6b5: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Malaysian government today announced an increase in the minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM2,000, effective June 2027.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim also said micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual revenues of less than RM50 million would be exempted from the increase to give them time to adapt their business models.
“The gap between workers’ productivity and wages must be narrowed, as the cost-of-living burden stems from incomes failing to keep pace with rising prices.
“This means more than four million workers will be covered by the new minimum wage rate,” he said while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat earlier today.
He also said the government will also introduce a minimum monthly salary of RM2,500 for semi-skilled workers and graduates as a starting point, as part of reforms to the country’s wage framework.
“The minimum wage only raises the income floor for workers, while wages for skilled workers remain disproportionate to their qualifications,” he said.

He also welcomed the commitment by government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) to raise their living wage benchmark from RM3,100 to RM3,400 a month which benefited about 230,000 workers.
Anwar said several major employers in the banking and oil and gas sectors had also introduced more reasonable wages, urging all private-sector employers to follow suit.

098e523f84e5abd2: KUALA LUMPUR: Kadar gaji minimum akan dinaikkan daripada RM1,700 kepada RM2,000 sebulan mulai Jun 2027, umum Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim.

afd1dec2effe86ac: PETALING JAYA: Kerajaan bercadang mengurangkan kadar cukai pendapatan individu pemastautin sebanyak satu mata peratusan, menurut Belanjawan Persekutuan 2027.

"Kenaikan pelepasan cukai dan pengurangan kadar cukai individu bakal memberi lebihan pendapatan boleh guna sehingga RM1,600 kepada kira-kira 5 juta pembayar cukai."
